summary: Range lights on Neebish Island in the St. Marys River, lit in 1895; the 1907 steel front tower came from Detroit in 1931 and stands unmanned.

structures.note: Built 1907 at Windmill Point, Detroit; erected on Neebish Island in 1931. Lengthened in 1919 with a 14 ft 8 in section; 50 ft to the focal plane (HAER).
The rear tower was moved 2,000 ft further back and replaced by a steel skeleton tower by 1958 (HAER).

access.note: Owned by the U.S. Coast Guard. The USLHS archive lists the station as not open to the public; LighthouseFriends says 'Grounds open, tower closed' and that it is best viewed from the water. The keepers' duplex is a private residence (LighthouseFriends).

corrections.why: LighthouseFriends, HAER and the USLHS name these range lights Lower Hay Lake, then Lower Nicolet (East and West). Middle Neebish Cut names a separate set of range lights (Stations 7 and 9, per HAER's 1930 specifications) and, in the 1921 Commissioner's report, the keepers' station.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The FY1921 Commissioner's report names Roger W. Campbell and W. S. Hall as keepers of 'Middle Neebish Cut Light Station'. The USLHS lists Campbell and Hall at this range (Lower Nicolet roster) and also keeps a separate Middle Neebish Cut record (Campbell 1918; Small 1925-1928 first assistant). The range lights were the Lower Hay Lake range in 1895 (LighthouseFriends; Light-House Board 1896) and the Lower Nicolet West range from 1931. Whether 'Middle Neebish Cut' and this station are one place is not settled by these sources; the story reports the 1921 events with that caveat.

resolved_conflicts.field: keepers: William S. Hall, principal keeper end year
resolved_conflicts.explanation: USLHS gives 1922 to 1931; LighthouseFriends gives 1922 to 1932. The USLHS line is kept, with the LighthouseFriends year in the note.
LighthouseFriends says Cook was promoted to head keeper and assigned to Little Rapids in 1941; the USLHS keeps him here as first assistant to 1943. Both are recorded.
LighthouseFriends has him as assistant 1925 to 1928, which the USLHS does not list; the USLHS has him as head keeper 1932 to 1933, which LighthouseFriends also gives. Both stints are kept.

HAER gives a 35 ft 4 in inward-sloping cylinder with a 14 ft 8 in section added in 1919, 50 ft to the focal plane; LighthouseFriends gives 42 ft for the original cylinder plus the 14 ft 8 in section. HAER's measured figures are used.
The USLHS archive lists the station 'Open to Public: No'; LighthouseFriends says 'Grounds open, tower closed'. The story gives both and does not choose between them.

The USLHS place record for Lower Nicolet West Range Front gives 'Year Established: 1959' and 'Type: Minor Aid to Navigation', which does not match the 1895 lights. The story does not use the 1959 date; it probably reflects the modern skeletal tower or a later record. Left for the editor.

notes_for_editor: Keepers: the roster lines come from the USLHS place record for Lower Nicolet West Range Front (NARA keeper registers via the Kraig Anderson inventory, per roster.py) and LighthouseFriends. The USLHS also keeps a Middle Neebish Cut record (cite 6) that lists Roger W. Campbell (1918) and William R. Small (1925-1928, first assistant) and Albert J. Davidson (to 1943); those are noted on this station only where the story says so. Only Campbell and Hall are confirmed in a primary text read here (FY1921 Commissioner's report, scan p. 667; the 1918-1923 Bulletin index lists the same names at Neebish Cut). The other names are not checked in a primary record, as the roster asks. The FY1921 report's printed page is not confirmed (the corpus shows 'p.62?'); cite by scan page until someone looks at the image. The Commissioner's report for 1931 and 1932 is not in the corpus; it is quoted only through HAER (second-hand, footnoted to HAER). LighthouseFriends is copyrighted: its facts are restated in our own words; its quotations are short. The rumrunner anecdote comes from LighthouseFriends citing a grandson and is second-hand; the story says 'reportedly'. The 1896 Light-House Board text is OCR ('Bange' for 'Range'), so the story paraphrases the range names rather than quoting them. The 1900 ice loss at middle light No. 12 (Lower Hay Lake Cut) was removed from the story: it is a single light, not these ranges, and the report does not tie it to this station. Height: LighthouseFriends gives the original cylinder as 42 feet, HAER as 35 ft 4 in; both are stated in the story. Fog signal: not in this station's story. Status: the USLHS place record gives 'Year Established: 1959' and 'Type: Minor Aid to Navigation'; not used. Position: the record's OSM point (46.324784, -84.175723) is about 80 m from LighthouseFriends (46.32465, -84.17647) and about 90 m from USLHS (46.325, -84.17667); left unchanged. No newspaper search was run for this station; the budget went to the corpus and HAER.
